english.title: Breach criminal behaviour order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without reasonable excuse,

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY ACT PERFORMED..) which you were prohibited from doing]_
(B)_[failed to **(..SPECIFY ACT NOT PERFORMED..) as required]_

by a criminal behaviour order made by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) on **(..SPECIFY DATE ORDER WAS MADE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 339(1) and (2) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
breached a criminal behaviour order
by doing anything he / she was prohibited from doing by the order OR
by failing to do anything he / she was required to do by the order

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: This offence applies to any breach of a criminal behaviour order after the Sentencing Act 2020 came in force on 1st December 2020, no matter when the order was issued. For breaches prior to that date, see offence H11451.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

The maximum penalty on summary conviction may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates' court, see section 339(2)(a) of the Sentencing Act 2020 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
